modules.description: Learn about intermediate processing work: receiving waste, matching documents and lots, checking conditions, and working safely during unloading. As of October 22, 2026, Japan's Ministry of the Environment aims to begin accepting workers in this sector in 2027 and says the skills-test details have not yet been decided; this material remains available as foundational learning.

lessons.caution: Do not accept or mix a lot whose identity does not match the facility's criteria.

checks.explanation: Identification links incoming material to process records and output.
options: So material can be traced through sorting and processing
So all loads can be mixed
To replace acceptance criteria
So weight records are unnecessary
checks.prompt: Why is the lot identity recorded at receiving?

options: Touch or open unfamiliar material
Combine containers to empty them quickly
Do not continue ordinary unloading. Hold the vehicle in a safe place, record the discrepancy, and request an inspection by the person in charge.
Skip recording it and move it to another area

checks.explanation: Sequence taught: Read the documents and facility acceptance criteria → Check the vehicle, container, and lot identities → Weigh or count according to procedure and record the actual result → Hold discrepancies and request a decision from the person in charge.
options: Read the documents and facility acceptance criteria

Weigh or count according to procedure and record the actual result

sections.body: This sector focuses on intermediate waste processing for recycling or appropriate treatment, not every type of collection work. Each facility has its own acceptance criteria and record format. Lot identity links incoming material to sorting, processing, and subsequent output.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before unloading, match the documents, vehicle or container number, declared material type, and weight from the scale. Record the actual result and time. If the type or quantity differs, hold acceptance or move it to the designated waiting area and ask the person in charge to decide.

Practice scenario: The documents say clean metal, but the load appears mixed with a sealed, unlabeled container.
Suggested response: Do not continue normal unloading. Hold the vehicle in a safe location, record the discrepancy, and request an inspection by the person in charge.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

sections.body: A load may contain sharp objects, batteries, cylinders, liquids, chemicals, or sealed items that do not match the initial description. It is unsafe to open or hand-sort unidentified material. The facility sets handling criteria and routes; workers must stop, keep others back, and request an assessment by trained staff.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Observe from a safe position without shaking or opening the container. Mark or cordon off the area as required, report the location, shape, markings, and any odor you notice, then wait for instructions. Do not touch liquid, damaged batteries, cylinders, or dusty materials unless assigned and properly protected.

Practice scenario: A swollen, odorous battery is visible on the conveyor while another worker is about to pick it up.
Suggested response: Give the stop signal as required, keep your distance, warn the crew, and report it immediately so trained staff can decide how to handle it.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

In the blind spot near the wheel

options: Stop unloading according to procedure, ask workers to move back to a safe zone, and continue only after the operator confirms the area is clear.
Touch or open unfamiliar material

Skip recording it and move it to another area

objectives: Menjaga jarak dari kendaraan serta memastikan zona bongkar dan komunikasi dengan operator aman.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.

lessons.response: Stop unloading according to procedure, ask the worker to move back to the safe zone, and resume only after the operator confirms the area is clear.
lessons.scenario: A driver starts raising the dump bed while a worker is still behind the truck reading a label.

sections.body: The unloading area has moving vehicles, raised dump beds, loads that may fall, and blind spots. Separate pedestrian routes and use a signaler to reduce the risk of being struck or crushed. Do not approach the dump bed or load until the operator gives the all-clear required by facility rules.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use the designated pedestrian routes and waiting zones. Make sure the operator can see the signaler; do not walk behind a vehicle or stand beneath a raised part. If someone enters the unloading zone, stop work using the method you were taught and alert the operator.

Practice scenario: A driver starts raising the dump bed while a worker is still behind the truck reading a label.
Suggested response: Stop unloading according to procedure, ask the worker to move back to the safe zone, and resume only after the operator confirms the area is clear.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Periksa tanda jalur dan zona tunggu
Pastikan pemberi isyarat serta operator siap
Jaga jarak dari kendaraan dan muatan saat bergerak
Hentikan proses dan laporkan orang atau muatan di zona berbahaya

modules.title: Receiving, Identification, and Area Safety

modules.description: Sort according to acceptance criteria and process destination, keep fractions separate, and report misplaced or mixed items.

lessons.caution: Do not sort by guessing or mix fractions just to empty a container.

checks.explanation: Facility criteria define the process destination and reduce mixing errors.
options: The stream label and applicable facility criteria
The item's color only
The nearest empty location
A worker's estimate based on its shape
checks.prompt: What should be consulted when deciding which sorting container to use?

checks.explanation: The closed container is not listed in the criteria; do not put it in the plastic fraction.
options: Touch or open unfamiliar material
Do not put it in the plastic fraction. Stop contact, isolate the area according to the rules, and report the item to the person in charge.
Combine containers to empty them quickly
Skip recording it and move it to another area
checks.prompt: At work, a closed aerosol container appears in a plastic stream, but it is not listed in the sorting criteria. What is the most appropriate action?

checks.explanation: Sequence taught: Read the stream label and applicable criteria → Inspect material before feeding it → Place it in the designated container or line → Hold and report unidentified material.
options: Inspect the material before feeding it in

Hold and report unidentified material

objectives: Memisahkan material sesuai label aliran dan kriteria fasilitas, serta menjaga bahan yang belum dikenali tetap tertahan.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Do not put it in the plastic fraction. Stop handling it, isolate the area as required, and report the item to the person in charge.
lessons.scenario: A sealed aerosol container appears in the plastic stream, but it is not listed in the sorting criteria.

sections.body: Sorting directs material to the appropriate process and prevents cross-contamination between fractions. Do not classify material by color or shape alone; use labels, acceptance lists, examples, and line instructions. Identify mixed material that cannot yet be sorted safely and handle it according to workplace rules.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Read the container label before adding material. Check items that look different; do not put batteries, sealed containers, or foreign materials into a regular stream. If the label is unreadable or the category is unclear, stop and ask for confirmation; record the location and visible type.

Practice scenario: A sealed aerosol container appears in the plastic stream, but it is not listed in the sorting criteria.
Suggested response: Do not put it in the plastic fraction. Stop handling it, isolate the area as required, and report the item to the person in charge.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Baca label aliran dan kriteria yang berlaku
Amati material sebelum memasukkannya
Tempatkan pada wadah atau jalur yang ditetapkan

Pull it by hand while the roller slows down
Use any stick without stopping the machine

options: Touch or open unfamiliar material

Stop and report any blockage or hazard

sections.body: Conveyors, rollers, cutters, and sorting equipment can catch clothing or crush hands. Keep unauthorized people out of the work area and use aids only as instructed. Never reach between rollers while the machine is moving; follow facility procedures for stopping and isolating equipment.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Stand in the marked position, use approved aids, and keep your arms and clothing away from moving parts. If material becomes stuck, a guard opens, or someone's hand enters a danger zone, stop the equipment according to the emergency procedure and call the operator. Do not pull out a blockage until the machine is safe.

Practice scenario: A piece of cloth is caught between rollers, and a worker is about to pull it out by hand while the machine runs slowly.
Suggested response: Do not reach in. Stop the line using the method you were taught, keep people back, and ask the operator to handle it once the machine is safe.

lessons.title: Conveyor and Sorting-Line Safety

lessons.caution: Do not move a container or change its label without updating the records.

checks.explanation: A mixed container needs assessment; its old label no longer describes its actual contents.
options: Stop filling, hold the container, and record the mixture

checks.explanation: Hold the item and report it so the supervisor can decide whether to sort it again or take another action.
options: Touch or open unfamiliar material
Combine containers to empty them quickly
Skip recording it and move it to another area

checks.explanation: Sequence taught: Prepare the correct container and destination label → Fill it only with a confirmed fraction → Record the lot, quantity, and container location → Hold and report any mixed fraction.
options: Prepare the correct container and destination label
Record the lot, quantity, and container location
Fill it only with a confirmed fraction
Hold and report the mixed fraction

lessons.response: Stop filling and hold the container. Record the contamination and ask whether it needs to be resorted or handled another way.
lessons.scenario: A metal container has a small amount of glass from the adjacent stream in it; the label still says clean metal.

sections.body: Sorted material may be compacted, wrapped, or prepared for the next processing stage. Containers and labels preserve the fraction identity, quantity, and destination process. If fractions are mixed or a marking is missing, hold the group so it is not fed into the wrong machine or switched during internal transfer.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Check the empty container, label, and destination before filling it. Record the time and lot in the facility's format, secure the specified lid or tie, and use a safe route for transfer. If the wrong material is added, do not pour it back without approval; mark the container and report the estimated amount and type of mixture.

Practice scenario: A metal container has a small amount of glass from the adjacent stream in it; the label still says clean metal.
Suggested response: Stop filling and hold the container. Record the contamination and ask whether it needs to be resorted or handled another way.

modules.description: Follow process-operation instructions and maintain equipment within your assigned role, including stopping and reporting abnormal conditions.

lessons.caution: Do not remove guards or repair a machine without training and the required isolation procedure.

options: Do not operate it; request an inspection according to procedure
Turn off the alarm light and start the process

Ask another worker to hold the door

checks.explanation: The equipment has not been declared safe; stop preparation and escalate the issue.
options: Do not operate the machine. Keep people away, notify the operator or supervisor, and wait for an inspection before starting the process.
Touch or open unfamiliar material
Combine containers to empty them quickly
Skip recording it and move it to another area

options: Read today's instructions and operator tasks
Report damage or abnormal signs
Operate only after the inspection confirms readiness
Check the guards, floor, and specified indicators

objectives: Memeriksa kondisi mesin, pelindung, jalur, dan tombol keselamatan sebelum menjalankan proses yang ditugaskan.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.

lessons.response: Do not start the machine. Keep people away, notify the operator or leader, and wait for an inspection before starting the process.
lessons.scenario: The compactor's warning light is on, and the guard door is not fully locked.

sections.body: Processing equipment may cut, crush, compact, or separate material. Pre-operation checks confirm guards are fitted, the area is clear, and measuring devices or indicators are working. Operate only equipment you have been trained to use; cleaning, repairs, and energy isolation must follow facility procedures and authorization.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use the startup checklist and report leaks, unusual sounds or vibration, and warning lights. Do not start a machine if a guard is open. Never put your hand in to clear a blockage or open an electrical panel.

Practice scenario: The compactor's warning light is on, and the guard door is not fully locked.
Suggested response: Do not start the machine. Keep people away, notify the operator or leader, and wait for an inspection before starting the process.

lessons.title: Pre-Operation Checks for Processing Equipment

lessons.caution: Do not change the sequence or mix lots to meet a production target.

checks.explanation: Lot records maintain traceability from receiving through output.
options: So output can be linked back to its material and process
So material from all sources can be mixed easily
To eliminate the need to weigh it
So the equipment can run without an operator
checks.prompt: Why must the lot identity be recorded on process output?

checks.explanation: The lot number does not match; hold the output and trace it before passing it on.
options: Touch or open unfamiliar material
Hold the output, record the visible mark, and ask the person in charge to trace the lot before it moves to the next process.
Combine containers to empty them quickly
Skip recording it and move it to another area
checks.prompt: At work, the lot mark on an output from a process does not match the incoming-material record. What is the most appropriate action?

checks.explanation: Sequence taught: Match the material lot to the process instructions → Follow the sequence and operator task limits → Record the time, result, and output identity → Hold abnormal results and request an inspection.
options: Follow the sequence and operator task limits
Match the material lot to the process instructions
Record the time, result, and output identity
Hold abnormal output and request an inspection
checks.prompt: In the “Following process order and recording results” workflow, what should be done next after the first step is complete?

dialogue.japanese: ロット番号が記録と違います。

objectives: Mengikuti urutan pengolahan yang ditetapkan serta mencatat lot, waktu, dan hasil sesuai format fasilitas.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Hold the output, record the visible markings, and ask the person in charge to trace the lot before moving it to the next process.
lessons.scenario: Output from a process has a lot mark that does not match the incoming-material record.

sections.body: Intermediate processing changes material's form or condition so it can be recovered or processed further. Each facility sets routes and parameters for its machines, including the sequence of incoming material and output. Actual records link incoming lots to output fractions and help identify deviations.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Verify material identity against the instructions before feeding it into the process, check required indicators, and record lot changes or weigh-ins. If output looks different, the machine stops, or identity is lost, hold the product and report it. Do not mix output from two processes to hide a weight difference.

Practice scenario: Output from a process has a lot mark that does not match the incoming-material record.
Suggested response: Hold the output, record the visible markings, and ask the person in charge to trace the lot before moving it to the next process.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

Ikuti urutan dan batas tugas operator

options: Touch or open unfamiliar material

options: Observe signs of damage from a safe position
Stop the equipment as instructed if the condition is hazardous

sections.body: Equipment can wear out, clog, leak, or develop electrical faults. Watch for designated warning signs, stop using equipment if there is a hazard, and notify maintenance staff. Cleaning, lubrication, part replacement, and energy isolation are restricted to authorized people following facility rules.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Record the machine number, time, problem location, sounds or indicators observed, and temporary action taken. Keep coworkers away if needed and post signs as required. Do not open a panel, insert a tool, or repeatedly restart the machine to clear an alarm.

Practice scenario: A line pump smells burnt and is vibrating more than usual while running.
Suggested response: Stop the equipment according to the emergency procedure, move away, and report the machine number and symptoms to the leader.

sections.body: Processed material may become feedstock for another stage, a reusable product, or residue that needs a different route. Facility records link incoming material weight and identity to the output and its next destination. Follow local procedures for record formats and data; do not guess the category or destination.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before transfer, check the label and process card, weigh or count as instructed, and record the actual result. If the quantity does not match or the destination marking is missing, hold the output in the designated location. Do not enter target figures in the records or move material elsewhere without permission.

Practice scenario: The output weight on the scale differs from the record, and the container's destination label has come off.
Suggested response: Hold the container, record the actual weight and any remaining information, and ask the person in charge to restore its destination before internal transfer.

sections.body: Storage areas may contain different materials with specific stacking limits, covers, and vehicle routes. Dust, liquid, or fragments can cause breathing problems, slippery floors, or contamination. Follow the facility's controls and equipment requirements; do not sweep, wash, or move a hazardous spill without instructions.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Place containers in marked areas, keep exit routes clear, and check lids and for leaks. If there is excessive dust or liquid escaping, warn others, keep your distance, and report the location and any known material type. Use protective equipment and procedures only if assigned to the task.

Practice scenario: Liquid is leaking from a storage drum near a floor drain, and the worker does not know what the drum contains.
Suggested response: Do not touch or wash away the liquid. Keep people back, mark the area as required, and contact authorized staff.

sections.body: Facility work spans processes and shifts. A clear handover states the location, lot number, machine status, recorded quantity, and next action. Factual records help the next team continue without mixing output or repeating completed steps. Hand over active hazards directly.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Complete the closing checklist, return tools to their locations, and mark lots still awaiting results. Tell the next person about damage, missing labels, or restricted areas. Do not mark unfinished work as complete; ask the recipient to repeat key information to confirm understanding.

Practice scenario: At the end of the shift, one output container is still awaiting lot verification, and the route near the machine has been marked off.
Suggested response: Keep the hold marker and route boundary in place, record the container number and reason, and hand over directly to the next shift and leader.
